question.text:
The area of the region, bounded by the curves $y=\sin ^{-1} x+x(1-x)$ and
$y=\sin ^{-1} x-x(1-x)$ in the first quadrant, is

solution.text:
$\sin ^{-1} x$ is defined, if $-1 \leq x \leq 1$ In first quadrant $0 \leq x \leq 1$ and $x(1-x) \geq 0$
$\therefore$
$y=\sin ^{-1} x+x(1-x)$
Lies above $y=\sin ^{-1} x-x(1-x)$
On solving, we get $2 x(1-x)=0$
$\Rightarrow \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad=0,1$
$\therefore$ Required area $=\int_{0}^{1}\left(y_{1}-y_{2}\right) d x$
$=\int_{0}^{1}\left[\left\{\sin ^{-1} x+x(1-x)\right\}\right.$
$\left.-\left\{\sin ^{-1} x-x(1-x)\right\}\right] d x$
$=2 \int_{0}^{1}\left(x-x^{2}\right) d x$
$=2\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}-\frac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{0}^{1}=2\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right)=\frac{1}{3}$
